videos.title: Grammy Is an American Award, Not a Nigerian Award Respect, The Headies & Chronicles of Afrobeats
videos.headline: Grammy Is an American Award, Not a Nigerian Award Respect, The Headies & Chronicles of Afrobeats
videos.description:
Bankulli sits down with Trending for a wide-ranging conversation on the Nigerian music industry, The Headies, the Grammys, respect, and his new project, Chronicles of Afrobeats.

In the conversation, Bankulli shares his thoughts on why “Grammy is an American award, not a Nigerian award” and why he believes Nigerians should pay more attention to The Headies and what the award represents for the Nigerian music industry.

He also speaks on the importance of respect within the music industry, emphasizing that respect is reciprocal, while reflecting on the recognition artists receive from major award platforms.

Bankulli also discusses Chronicles of Afrobeats and the importance of documenting and preserving the story of Afrobeats.

He weighs in on the criticism surrounding The Headies, urging people not to be too harsh on the awards, especially considering that The Headies is only about 20 years old, while the Grammys has been around for over 60 years.

From Ayra Starr and Wizkid to the evolution of Afrobeats and the future of Nigerian music, Bankulli gives his perspective on the industry and the people shaping it.

Watch the full conversation and let us know what you think.

videos.title: How Salem King Became Nigeria's Ultimate Creator
videos.headline: How Salem King Became Nigeria's Ultimate Creator
videos.description:
​@salemkinging didn’t set out to become a full-time creator.

The son of ministers, Salem grew up in a home that encouraged curiosity, reading and asking questions. He went on to study Economics at university before entering the world of real estate, where he sold some of the most expensive properties in Nigeria’s most exclusive neighbourhoods.

Then, on the side, he started making content.

What began as a creative experiment quickly turned into something much bigger. His content found an audience, went viral and opened up opportunities he hadn't expected. As his platform grew, Salem began teaching others what he had learnt, sharing his knowledge through a series of classes designed to help aspiring creators build their confidence and find their voice.

Eventually, he made the decision to leave his job and pursue content creation full-time.

Today, Salem King is building the Creatorium franchise and positioning himself at the centre of Nigeria's rapidly evolving creator economy.

In this episode, we talk about his childhood, his journey from Economics to real estate, the moment he discovered the power of content, what going viral really changed, leaving a conventional career behind and what it takes to build a sustainable life as a creator.

videos.title: How Ladipoe Became One of Nigeria's Best Rappers
videos.headline: How Ladipoe Became One of Nigeria's Best Rappers
videos.description:
​@LadipoeLOTR  studied Biology and Chemistry at the University of North Carolina before moving back home to Nigeria, hoping to make the big break as a Recording Artist. 

He was in luck. His mother found a kindred spirit: another rapper’s mother while taking a course at the Lagos Business School. That rapper was Wale “Tec” Davies of @showdemcamp. Tec felt his bars and invited him into a creative circle, which incubated acts like Show Dem Camp, Funbi, @temidollfacevevo4701, @temsbaby, and more. 

Poe announced his presence on “Feel Alright”- a collab with SDC and @Bojdrb, which has been credited as being a precursor to the iconic Palm Wine Music series. 

Don Jazzy's @MavinRecords  came calling, and Poe vowed to make the best of the opportunity. Nearly 10 years later, he’s found the type of mainstream appeal that once seemed out of reach. This year, he released "Revival", one of the year’s best releases, highlighting why he’s one of the country’s most beloved artists.  

On this episode of Overnight Success, he takes us on the long journey from medical professional to one of the country's premier rappers.

videos.description:
Award-winning actress Genoveva Umeh is a village girl at heart, and she’s not afraid to own it.

On this episode of One More Thing, Genoveva talks about growing up in Enugu, moving to London at 11, and choosing acting after studying law. She shares what drives her to tell authentic African stories, how she approaches auditions, and the lessons that have shaped her career, from Blood Sisters to Breath of Life and her latest project, Tele X Zikora.
 
She also opens up about the mantra that keeps her grounded, why she believes actors should never outgrow auditions, and what she thinks separates confidence from arrogance. Plus, find out why she describes her biggest green flag as someone who “feels like home.”

Watch and enjoy!

videos.title: Can Migration Consulting Really Pay More Than Medicine? | Wakawaka Doctor on MY DAILY 2K
videos.headline: Can Migration Consulting Really Pay More Than Medicine? | Wakawaka Doctor on MY DAILY 2K
videos.description:
In this episode of #MYDAILY2K medical doctor, travel consultant, and global mobility advocate Wakawaka Doctor opens up about balancing a demanding 12-year medical career with building one of the continent's most trusted migration platforms.

From starting out giving free travel advice during the pandemic to structuring a paid advisory ecosystem, he discusses: 
• How clinical diagnostic skills like research, active listening, and empathy translate directly into migration consulting 
• Why he resisted monetizing his advice for years and the reality of overcoming underpricing 
• A behind-the-scenes look at the "chaos with a sprinkle of beauty" in his daily routine 
• The weight of responsibility when guiding people through life-altering relocation decisions
• His personal definition of luxury and the biggest lessons learned along the way
